title: Al fin y al cabo: después de todo, en definitiva

sections.content: Al fin y al cabo (after all, when all is said and done) puts a conclusion in perspective -- it reminds the reader of an underlying truth that outweighs the details just given. It's a natural way to step back and state what really matters. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Al fin y al cabo, la propia independencia de Panamá de Colombia en 1903 había estado íntimamente ligada a los intereses de Washington en construir el canal.
items.english: After all, Panama's own 1903 independence from Colombia had been closely tied to Washington's interest in building the canal.

items.spanish: Panamá asumió la operación del canal sin mayores contratiempos, al fin y al cabo demostrando una capacidad técnica que pocos análisis previos le habían reconocido.
items.english: Panama took over operation of the canal without major setbacks, after all demonstrating a technical capacity that few earlier analyses had credited it with.

items.spanish: Al fin y al cabo, este curso recorrió un largo camino desde las sociedades precolombinas hasta la democratización.
items.english: After all, this course covered a long road from pre-Columbian societies to democratization.

items.spanish: Al fin y al cabo, el siglo XX de la región no terminó con un solo final, sino con este traspaso silencioso de soberanía.
items.english: When all is said and done, the region's twentieth century did not end with a single ending, but with this quiet transfer of sovereignty.

sections.content: Al fin y al cabo usually opens or closes a sentence, set off by a comma, and works best as a genuine final word on a topic -- not just any transition, but the point you want the reader to remember above the rest.
